topology.description: The same world scalar field is sampled at the left and right head surface. Rectified lateral contrast drives mirrored sensory and anterior premotor LIF channels, then bilaterally paired subsets of existing A1-A3 motor identities and named muscle fibers. Segment-scaled neural drive makes asymmetric contraction span the anterior pivot instead of applying a single body hinge; left-right activation difference enters active-curvature physics while axial force and continuous contact remain the frozen axial-v1 path.

connections.edge: bilateral head field samples -> rectified sensory contrast

connections.evidence: Berni et al. 2015, Current Biology 25:1817-1828; Pulver et al. 2015, Journal of Neurophysiology 113:3322-3336
connections.allowed_use: relative left-right anterior circuit topology only

connections.edge: anterior asymmetric contraction spans T3-A3 with an A1 peak
connections.evidence: Lahiri et al. 2011, PLOS ONE 6:e23180, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0023180, Fig. 9 and Methods
connections.allowed_use: relative segment support and A1-peak ordering only; not L1 absolute amplitude

connections.edge: side-resolved motor identities -> A1-A3 named fibers
connections.stage: L1 for A1 identity; anatomy-derived homology for A2-A3
connections.allowed_use: identity event routing with original per-edge provenance

limitations: This is not a reconstructed complete L1 steering connectome.
The field modality and rectified opponent transform are generic research transduction, not an identified receptor pathway.
A1-A3 steering delays, segment current scales, LIF currents, and active-curvature gain are fitted parameters.
Individual L1 muscle moment arms and force gains remain unavailable; yaw uses a reduced side-activation curvature constraint.
A1 public MN-to-muscle coverage is left-right incomplete; steering uses only muscle numbers mapped on both sides and retains a small documented residual axial-force asymmetry.
The current atlas has no T3 MN-to-muscle projection; no T3 motor identity is invented, and the T3-A1 boundary bends only through adjacent real A1 activation.
The scalar field creates sensory input only and never supplies a desired turn direction or heading.

parameter_provenance.objective: Preserve frozen axial-v1 straight locomotion at zero lateral contrast while mirrored field gradients produce stable mirrored yaw and a distributed T3-A3 anterior pivot through A1-A3 side activation, with A1 strongest.
parameter_provenance.uncertainty: No numeric current, delay, segment scale, contrast gain, active-curvature gain, or scalar-field gradient is asserted as measured L1 biology. Lahiri et al. constrains relative support and ordering from L2, not L1 amplitude.

environment.note: The field is evaluated from current world positions every dt; it does not inspect neural, muscle, or requested movement state.

mechanics.yaw_path: left-right named-fiber activation difference -> active curvature XPBD constraint

required_gates: positive and negative lateral field gradients produce mirrored heading and lateral displacement
uniform field preserves frozen axial-v1 trajectory within numerical tolerance
sensory, motor-neuron, and muscle lesions attenuate the corresponding steering response
every steering-driven active fiber force traces to field sample, sensory spike, premotor spike, and motor spike
axial-v1 forward calibration and backward diagnostic behavior remain unchanged
turning remains within segment extension, chord-ratio, local-bend, and integrated-slip rejection gates
steering-excess curvature spans all four T3-A1 through A3-A4 pivot joints, peaks adjacent to A1, and passes hinge-concentration gates
validation.claim_limit: Axial-v1-integrated bilateral steering research approximation; not an independently validated L1 steering connectome or measured muscle moment-arm model.
